newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Heavyweights fuel Zimbabwe industrials higher.
newsitem.headline: Heavyweights fuel Zimbabwe industrials higher.

text.p: Zimbabwe industrial shares jumped to yet another new high on Monday, driven mainly by gains in heavyweights Meikles and Delta.
Dealers said trade had been active with many investors moving out of second-tier stocks ahead of new issues, due over the next few weeks and for which they wanted funds.
"It was another new record and was mainly driven by Meikles and Delta. A lot of people are climbing out of second-tier stocks to go into the new issues," one dealer said.
He added that some foreigners were starting to offload Delta stock and taking profit.
Dealers said Randalls' listing and new share issue in March was viewed positively and was likely to be very well-supported.
The 57-share industrial index added 32.84 points to 10,706.87.
Delta put on 10 cents to 1,720 cents, Meikles jumped 75 cents to 2,450 and Zimplow rose 120 cents to 800.
Trading in mining shares was quiet with dull sentiment, due to a slight decline in the bullion price and dampened further by profit warnings issued by Falgold and Falcon.
"The Falcon cautionaries will affect the mining index further but it depends more on how it trades, when it trades," a dealer said.
Falcon was quoted lower at 500/1,000 cents per share from a previous closing price of 1,300 cents, but not traded. Falgold was also lower at 30/50 cents per share from 105 cents, but untraded.
Ashanti added 500 cents to 9,500 cents. The seven-share mining index closed 3.95 points up at 886.24.
